title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): Frequently asked questions about OpenJDK remote code execution vulnerability
content_md: Java4Shell is a flaw in how Java decodes Base64 data. Calif, which found it, says it can let attackers run code on widely used Java applications without logging in. Oracle released fixed Java builds on November 17, and Calif is withholding its exploits for individual applications for now. Key takeaways CVE-2026-114938, dubbed Java4Shell, is an OpenJDK memory corruption vulnerability that Oracle scores 8.1 on CVSS 3.1, and Calif says its testing showed attackers could run code without logging in on applications such as Atlassian Jira and Jenkins. As of November 17, Tenable is not aware of any reports that attackers have exploited this flaw, though Calif has published a PoC that triggers the bug without taking control of the system and a second researcher reports building a working exploit. Oracle released fixed builds on November 17, and according to Calif, only systems running an affected Java version on x86-64 processors that support AVX-512 VBMI can be affected. Background Tenable's Research Special Operations (RSO) team has compiled this blog to answer Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) regarding Java4Shell, a vulnerability in OpenJDK that was patched on November 17, 2026. FAQ When was Java4Shell first disclosed? On November 17, security firm Calif said on X that it had found and reported the flaw, and that details of Java4Shell, as Calif named it, had leaked ahead of a fix.
